source_ref: OSF dqw9f (public node; API reports no node licence): Supplemental Studies/Study S1a Data and Code/Study S1a Data.sav (https://osf.io/download/5p78v/, sha256 ceefe3a63ccdf3da75a45c16b8097517085cf64453f9fb2b8118646534503f33) and Supplemental Studies/Study S2b Data and Code/Study S2b Data.sav (https://osf.io/download/6501ed786d1e89617115155a/, sha256 37cf92d0603caa457eb098eec7a1cb291558292e17346e26a03eb25054ba05dd) -- SPSS variable and value labels of elaborate1-2/know1-2/values1-2/important1-2 (S1a) and elab1-2/know1-2/value1-2/import1-2 (S2b); data/wallace_2026_mindsets.py (reflection.csv spec) for the code derivation. Paper: Wallace, Murphy, Hernandez-Colmenares & Fujita (2026) JPSP 130(2) 291-307, doi:10.1037/pspi0000498.
note: Level 1, both label levels read (.sav files copied from the batch_655 wallace_2026_mcm_culture cache; sha256s match the batch_644-657 records). CODE DERIVATION: reflection.csv spec maps {m}{k} -> {m}_item{k} for m in elaborate/know/values/important, k in 1,2, studies S1a and S2b only, no '-' prefix, so no recode and no itemcov_recoded column: a fixed number-preserving rename, exempt from Step 5b, no verification files. S1a: the source columns elaborate1..important2 carry the variable and value labels directly. S2b: the script reads elaborate1/2, values1/2, important1/2, which are UNLABELLED columns appended at the end of the file; the labelled originals are elab1/2, value1/2, import1/2, and each pair is identical in all 340 rows (checked), so the labels transfer; know1/2 are read directly and are labelled. The S1a and S2b variable labels are character-identical item by item, as are the value labels, so item_text ships the one wording unprefixed (no per-study split needed). values_item1 reads 'the response', values_item2 'the answer' -- verbatim, not harmonised. Item pairs share wording: per the .sav column order in both files, each _item1 follows the belief statement IQbelief1T1 ('You have a certain amount of intelligence, and you can't really do much to change it.') and each _item2 follows IQbelief1T2 ('Your intelligence is something about you that you can't change very much.'); 'the topic we just asked you about' refers to that statement. Stated in public_note, not written into item_text (batch_647 wallace_2026_certain convention). OPTIONS: value labels 1='1 - Not at all', 2..6 bare digits, 7='7 - Very much' for all 8 items in both files; shipped as 'Not at all'/'Very much' with the number prefixes stripped (sibling convention); 2-6 blank, not padded. Sanity counts (not required for the exemption): live 4624 rows = 578 ids x 8; cov_study 2 = S1a (238 ids, 1904 rows), 6 = S2b (340 ids, 2720 rows); all 16 study x item resp-count vectors equal the source exactly, e.g. S1a elaborate1 2/13/24/42/62/44/51, S2b know1 6/13/37/76/122/52/34, S2b important2 15/19/17/54/85/91/59; every item used all 7 levels in both studies. No instructions or lead-in text in either .sav; the S1a .sps contains no text for these items and the S2b .sps download returns an OSF 500 error body (not needed). Instructions left blank. Rights: study-authored items; no fee, permission, NC or redistribution clause located (silence = permission). Not in instrument_rights_register.csv; no register row written.
public_note: Each rating was asked right after an intelligence-belief statement and refers back to it: the _item1 ratings follow You have a certain amount of intelligence, and you can't really do much to change it. and the _item2 ratings follow Your intelligence is something about you that you can't change very much., so the paired items share their wording.
